thread:
pagerbot: Pager: increased 5xx rate + p95 latency spike observed for inference cluster in us-east-1a (route: /v1/generate). Alerting thresholds crossed (5xx > 2% over 5m).

maya_oncall: seeing it, joining. pulling metrics now.

jon_eng: confirmed RPC timeouts to a subset of instances in us-east-1a, kernel tx drops on a few hosts in the podset. Logs show repeated `ENETUNREACH` and `connection refused` from client side.

maya_oncall: runbook step 1 — isolate problem: disabling new LB stickiness to allow redistribution. `curl https://internal-lb/api/health` shows 12% unhealthy.

opsbot: Autoscaler triggered +2 replicas but they are failing health checks (startup success, then net errors).

maya_oncall: probable local resolver/resolver-proxy backlog. TTLs look normal but we have resolver timeouts ~600ms. Starting immediate mitigation: 1) shift 30% traffic to us-east-1b via routing policy, 2) lower resolver TTL at edge to 5s to avoid long sticky failures, 3) drain obviously failing nodes.

jon_eng: executing drain: `kubectl drain inference-g5-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on the 3 bad nodes. I've pinned traffic away from those instances in the LB.

maya_oncall: patching routing policy: `redwoodctl route adjust --cluster us-east --az us-east-1b --pct 30` — done. Confirming downstream kv-cache population hit due to reroutes (kvcache regen visible).

sre_lead: recommend temporary fallback to smaller model variant for requests that hit p95 timeouts to reduce end-to-end latency while we stabilize. Suggest toggling canary fallback rule.

maya_oncall: enabled model-fallback for critical routes. p95 for those routes dropped ~120ms after change. Overall 5xx rate down from 2.6% -> 0.9%.

nina_cs: CS: customers reporting increased latencies and a handful of 500s. Drafting status page note: short impact window, engineering investigating, mitigation in progress. Will post after you give green.

jon_eng: digging into host NIC counters — tx_dropped, tx_errors spiked coincident with resolver timeouts. Kicking a soft NIC reset on two hosts as a last-ditch before eviction: `ethtool -s eth0 speed 10000 autoneg on` then `ip link set dev eth0 down; ip link set dev eth0 up`.

maya_oncall: NIC reset succeeded on host a-3 and a-7, health checks recovered for those. One host still flapping, leaving drained.

opsbot: Traffic redistribution to us-east-1b holding stable at 30%. No cross-region failover needed.

sre_lead: next steps: continue to monitor for 30m, keep kvcache warmers on to avoid regen storm, and prepare capacity increase in us-east-1b if sustained. Also open a ticket with cloud provider for host NIC telemetry.

maya_oncall: handing off to next on-call. Summary for handoff: - incident start 1768465012; root symptoms: resolver/backplane pressure + NIC tx errors causing instance health-check failures; mitigations done: drained bad nodes, soft NIC resets, routing shift 30%->us-east-1b, enabled model fallback, lowered edge resolver TTL to 5s, kvcache warmers enabled; current status: 5xx down to 0.9%, p95 improved but still ~150ms above baseline on some routes; customers: CS draft ready, few customers impacted, no major outage.

maya_oncall: @leo_oncall please take it from here, I'll put exact commands and node IDs in the follow-up runbook entry. :white_check_mark:

leo_oncall: taking over. I'll keep the routing policy as-is for now and coordinate with cloud provider and SRE to validate NIC flakiness. Noted to post status page: "Mitigation in progress, partial route redistribution, reduced errors".

nina_cs: posting status now. ETA for next update 30m. cc @customers 

jon_eng: saved diagnostic logs to `s3://redwood-incident-logs/1768465012/` including tcpdump and kernel counters, and linked to runbook entry.

maya_oncall: adding follow-up action items: 1) provider ticket + host telemetry, 2) post-incident review scheduled, 3) consider resolver-proxy scaling and backpressure controls.

leo_oncall: ack. I'll reopen if error rate creeps or host flapping resumes.

pagerbot: Incident annotated: mitigation actions recorded, incident moved to monitoring state.
